notes: This updated codebook includes tightened definitions, exclusion rules to resolve ambiguity between adjacent labels, and worked examples with more concrete text. Each label has a distinct definition, clarification, and negative clarification to ensure clear annotation.

codes.name: Capacity and Resources
codes.definition: Availability or lack of physical, financial, human, or spatial resources.
codes.negative_clarification: Excludes discussions about policy solutions or economic implications.

positive_examples.text: @Adventure_Ost @ErikMarquardt Leben diese Migranten in Hotels mit all-you-can-eat?  #Vollpfosten
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Capacity and Resources because the tweet discusses migrants' living conditions, which relates to resource availability.

negative_examples.text: @WhiteHouse Illegals pick our fruits and veggies!  And work at his golf courses!
negative_examples.why: Not annotated with Capacity and Resources because it focuses on economic implications rather than resource availability.

codes.name: Crime and Punishment
codes.definition: Violations of laws, including crimes, policing, punishment, and enforcement.
codes.negative_clarification: Excludes discussions about policy solutions or judicial processes.

positive_examples.text: @RedXantusiidae @SenSanders The study is looking at the crime rates of 100,000 people in each subpopulation...
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Crime and Punishment because it discusses crime rates and law enforcement.

negative_examples.why: Not annotated with Crime and Punishment because it discusses policy stances rather than crime or punishment.
